ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, given that the area of the square $ABCD$ is 64 square centimeters and $DE = 10$ cm, what is the length of $CE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Since the area of square ABCD is 64 square centimeters, $\therefore$ $\angle ADC=90^\circ$ and $DC=8$ cm. Since $DE=10$ cm, $\therefore$ $CE=\sqrt{DE^{2}+DC^{2}}=\sqrt{8^{2}+10^{2}}=\boxed{2\sqrt{41}}$ (cm).

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The diagram shows square ABCD on the left, with A at the upper-left, B at the lower-left, C at the lower-right, and D at the upper-right. Segment DE extends horizontally to the right from D to E. Segment DC is vertical, and segment CE is slanted from C up to E, forming triangle DCE. Since DC is vertical and DE is horizontal, triangle DCE is right-angled at D. Reasoning: The area of square ABCD is 64 cm^2, so each side of the square is sqrt(64) = 8 cm. Thus DC = 8 cm. Given DE = 10 cm, in right triangle DCE, CE is the hypotenuse. By the Pythagorean theorem, CE = sqrt(DC^2 + DE^2) = sqrt(8^2 + 10^2) = sqrt(64 + 100) = sqrt(164) = 2sqrt(41) cm.
